newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns against grain output complacency.
newsitem.headline: China warns against grain output complacency.

text.p: China's top leaders warned local officials on Monday against complacency in grain production, telling them a bumper harvest last year did not guarantee a similar feat in 1997.

A good harvest was important to ensure stability in rural areas, which are home to an estimated 800 million of China's 1.2 billion people, Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin told a conference in Beijing on agriculture.
"Leaders must not be blinded by optimism because of good grain harvests during the past few years," state television quoted Jiang as saying.
China has forecast a record grain harvest of 480 million tonnes for 1996, up from a previous record of 466 million tonnes the previous year.

Officials have said they hope to repeat last year's bumper harvest in 1997 but have said a sharp increase was unlikely because the area expected to be planted with grain would be similar, or even slightly lower, than 1996.
"We must make a full appraisal of the arduousness of increasing this year's grain output, and never treat it lightly," Jiang was quoted as saying.

He stressed the importance of ensuring a sustained and steady increase in output of grain and other major farm products, boosting farmers' incomes, stepping up construction of reservoirs and dams and maintaining the stability of rural society.
China's economic tsar, Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji, told the conference that grain production needed more effort, with average per capita output of 390 kg no higher than the high water mark set in 1984.
"China's grain is not in surplus," Zhu warned.
China's communist leaders have long been concerned to ensure ample grain harvests after more than 28 million people starved to death in the Great Leap Forward of the late 1950s.
China is faced with the task of feeding one fifth of the world's population -- or 1.2 billion people -- on just seven percent of its arable land.
